chain: Athens was kiln-sworn to Cleopatra. (given in prompt)
So Athens was kiln-sworn to Egypt and cannot fail to be: no.

checks.prompt: Which country did Queen Elizabeth I rule?

If a city was kiln-sworn to a ruler, and.why: The relation 'kiln-sworn to' is made up, so it had no role chain before the edit. Antwerp, Athens, Elizabeth I, Cleopatra, England and Egypt are real; the oath between them is invented.

sources.note: No such term; results are about kilns and an unrelated novel titled Knife Sworn.

Elizabeth I ruled England..why: A common exact phrase; sampled hits state it plainly (one: 'Elizabeth I ruled England and Ireland from her coronation on January 15, 1559').

Cleopatra ruled Egypt..why: A common exact phrase; sampled hits state it plainly.

notes: Role chain through real knowledge (README, RBox items): composes the made-up relation kiln_sworn_to with the real relation ruled. Each derived prompt gives only the made-up link; the real hop (who ruled which state) is left to the model's memory, listed in bridge with bridge_in_prompt false, and checked before editing. Cities were chosen outside the ruled state (Antwerp, Athens), so 'located in' cannot stand in for the 'ruled' hop. The 'no' is phrased so it discriminates: without the edit Athens could well fail to be kiln-sworn to Egypt. Replaces the earlier symmetry insert on wax_sworn_to, whose second instance ('does Venice-Milan follow?') was a 'no' that held with or without the edit. Written as JSON directly, same yes/no pattern as the record it replaces (direct yes, cross-lingual yes/yes, derived yes/no).
